title: trace/v1 event (one JSONL line = one event)
description: One edge in the append-only Decision-Evidence trace ledger. See docs/protocols/trace-v1.md. A ledger is a sequence of these objects, one per line (JSONL); this schema validates a single event object, not the file as a whole. Corrections are new events carrying `supersedes_event_id` -- a conformant writer/reader MUST NOT rewrite or delete a past line. `supersedes_event_id` MUST NOT equal this event's own `event_id` (a self-reference) -- not expressible as a schema constraint in this repo's validator subset (it would require comparing two sibling field values, not a fixed const), so it is enforced in verify-fixtures.mjs instead; see the `invalid-self-supersedes` fixture.

allOf.description: Per-relation required fields (docs/protocols/trace-v1.md section 3's identity table). Presence here is a structural MUST; verify-fixtures.mjs additionally cross-checks from_ref/to_ref's logical_id against task_run_id/session_id's "task_run:<id>"/"session:<id>" convention for session_bound and usage_imported, which isn't expressible as a schema constraint (comparing one field's value against another field's value, not a fixed const).

usage_imported additionally requires payload.window.{since,until} -- see the named identity exception in section 3: these two fields participate in event_id identity even though payload as a whole does not.

event_id.description: Deterministic, idempotent identity: "tr1_" + lowercase hex sha256 of the RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization of {schema: "trace/v1", relation, identity}, where `identity` is the relation-specific field subset defined in docs/protocols/trace-v1.md section 3. A reader MUST recompute this and reject the event if it does not match the declared value.

relation.description: Closed set (16 values). The names `incident_observed` and `rolled_back_to` are reserved for a future version in documentation only (see docs/protocols/trace-v1.md) -- they are NOT enum members here (sol architect-review 3rd round must1: an earlier draft listed them as valid enum members while a verify-fixtures.mjs semantic check unconditionally rejected any event using either, a schema/semantic split with no benefit -- v1 never defined an identity/payload shape for them, so there is nothing for the schema to accept in the first place). Emitting either value today is a plain enum violation, exactly like any other unrecognized string.

occurred_at.description: UTC only. This ledger has no concept of a local-offset timestamp -- every writer MUST convert to UTC and render with a literal "Z" suffix before emitting.

causation_event_id.description: event_id of the event that caused this one (a different relationship than supersedes_event_id, which is about correction, not causation).

payload.description: Relation-specific body. Left unconstrained here (each relation defines its own shape informally in docs/protocols/trace-v1.md); it is deliberately excluded from the event_id identity computation as a whole so an emitter-version bump or additional diagnostic field never changes an event's id. A relation MAY still name specific payload sub-fields as identity inputs (see usage_imported's window.since/window.until in the protocol doc) -- that is a named exception per relation, not a general inclusion of payload.

supersedes_event_id.description: event_id of the event this one corrects. The superseded event is never rewritten or removed -- both rows remain in the ledger permanently. A reader MAY find no event with this id in the segment it has loaded (the original could be in an earlier ledger segment/file it hasn't read); that MUST NOT be treated as a validation failure at the single-event level (see docs/protocols/trace-v1.md section 9).

ref.description: Identifies one endpoint of an edge. An artifact_revision node's logical_id is the bare logical id (e.g. "intent.yaml"); its content_digest pins one specific revision, together forming the <logical_id>@sha256:<digest> two-part node identity described in the platform's Decision-Evidence Graph design. A runtime_entity node (a run, a session, a release, ...) has no content revision, so content_digest is absent and logical_id alone (e.g. "run:<id>", "session:<id>") is the whole identity.

actor.description: actor.id is audit provenance ('who/what recorded this fact'), not a metrics dimension -- see docs/protocols/trace-v1.md's actor.id note. It MUST NOT be used as a group-by/aggregation axis in a projection built from this ledger.
